tasks.short: Find and refile the customer card, record the service type, date, licence plate and mileage, take the customer's contact and consent, find customers due for service, check the reminder list, send reminders, phone customers without e-mail, have customers book, and enter the bookings.

steps.what: Service attendant finds the customer's card in the card box and files it back after each service
Service attendant maintains customer records by recording the service type, date, licence plate and mileage of each service
Customer gives a mobile number or e-mail address and agrees to service reminders
Service attendant goes through the cards to find customers due for service
Service attendant checks the due list: service due, due date and contact for each customer

Service attendant follows up with reminders of services due; after the change the system sends each checked reminder (customer name, licence plate, service due, due date and booking link) by text or e-mail to the number or address the customer gave
Service attendant phones regular customers who have no e-mail or mobile number
Customer phones back or uses the booking link to book the service
Service attendant enters the service bookings in the agenda

tasks.design: At the till the attendant records each service against the licence plate: the sale already carries the service type and date, the attendant types the plate and mileage, and the till and service system sets the next due date from the station's interval for that service type, so no card box is kept or searched. The customer gives a mobile number or e-mail address and agrees to reminders. Each week the system lists customers due from those records; the attendant checks the list, and only then each checked reminder (name, plate, service due, due date, booking link) goes by text or e-mail to the contact the customer gave. Regulars without a number or address still get a call. Bookings made through the link land in the agenda.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer cards were paper and reminders were phone calls one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Garage systems compute due dates from service records and send reminders with booking links.
tasks.still_hard: Older regulars expect a personal call.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which regular will only book if asked in person.
tasks.altitude: The attendant checks reminders instead of finding and calling every customer.

evidence.claim: Garage service systems can compute due dates from service records and send reminders with booking links.
Service reminders to existing customers use their contact details, which are personal data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the service done to the service booked; the service itself is outside.

Input contract: the reminder's source is the service record from s2 (service type and date from the till sale, plate and mileage typed by the attendant, next due date from the station's interval per service type); its destination is the mobile number or e-mail address the customer gave with consent in s3; fallback is a call.

s1 is gone because no card box is kept; s2 keeps half because the sale already gives service type and date and only plate and mileage are typed; s4 keeps 10 for opening the weekly list; s9 keeps 40 for bookings made by phone.
Customers' time to give contact details and book through the link is shown in s3 and s8 and priced as customer time.
Calls to regulars without e-mail or mobile stay.
research_questions: Do more customers return for service when due?

incremental.description: Service attendant collects e-mail addresses and mobile numbers at the till.
Customers book through the reminder link.

approvals.approved_version: The reminder list exactly as checked by the attendant in s5: for each listed customer the name, licence plate, service due, due date and booking link, sent once by text or e-mail to the contact the customer gave in s3; customers the attendant removes get nothing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many older regulars who need calls and few contact details; high: most customers give a mobile number or e-mail.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hear the customer's question, give directions from local knowledge, look up road works and closures, and show the route on a map.

steps.what: Customer asks about the road or route
Service attendant provides customers with information about local roads or highways
Service attendant searches road works and closures on websites while the customer waits
Service attendant draws the route on a paper map

tasks.design: A screen at the counter shows live road works, closures and traffic for the area from the public traffic feed, so the attendant reads the item for the customer's road instead of searching websites while the customer waits. A QR code opens the route in the customer's own navigation app, so fewer routes are drawn on paper maps. Giving directions from local knowledge does not change and keeps its full time.
tasks.previous_blocker: Road works were searched on websites while the customer waited, or remembered, and routes were drawn on paper maps.
tasks.enabler_now: Public traffic feeds and navigation apps give live road information.
tasks.still_hard: Local shortcuts and tricky junctions are not on any screen.
tasks.human_edge: Warning a caravan driver about a low bridge the app ignores.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and map drawing; directions stay.

reach.learn: Whether the counter screen is used.

evidence.claim: Public traffic feeds show road works, closures and traffic; navigation apps open routes from a link.

assumptions: Boundary: from the customer's question to the route shown; selling maps is outside.
Input contract: road information from the public traffic feed; fallback is local knowledge and paper maps.
s2 keeps its full time: directions from local knowledge do not change.
s3 keeps 60: the website search is removed, but reading the item for the customer's road and explaining it stay.
s4 keeps 70: about 30% of customers take the QR route instead of a drawn map; the rest still get the paper map.
Customers open the route on their phone in about the time it took to look at the map; priced as customer time.
research_questions: Do customers use the QR route?

incremental.description: Service attendant checks the counter screen works each morning.
Customers open the route on their own phone.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly local regulars who ask for local directions; high: a motorway station with many travellers using the screen and QR route.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The service attendant keeps serving customers and giving local advice; paper cards, reminder calls and paper maps shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An attendant with more time for customers at the pump and counter.
